official_scope: identification and classification of rocks and minerals
design_notes: Concept density varies by topic: 10–14 concepts per topic. Mineral ID is deliberately split into separate diagnostic property concepts to allow fine-grained clinic remediation. Rock ID keeps hand-sample and thin-section identification separate from genetic process topics to avoid duplicate concept ownership. Topics 5–7 were kept dense with process-specific atomic concepts; topic 8 remains leaner but covers cycle, economic, and environmental applications. No topic left as a stub.

concepts.title: Definition of a mineral
concepts.description: Identify the five criteria (naturally occurring, inorganic, solid, ordered internal structure, definite chemical composition) and apply them to classify substances as minerals or not.

concepts.title: Luster types and metallic/nonmetallic division
concepts.description: Distinguish metallic, submetallic, vitreous, resinous, pearly, greasy, silky, adamantine, and dull lusters in hand specimens.

concepts.title: Mohs hardness scale and field hardness tests
concepts.description: Apply the Mohs scale (1–10) and common hardness indicators to determine relative hardness and discriminate minerals.

concepts.title: Cleavage vs fracture and cleavage quality
concepts.description: Distinguish cleavage planes from fracture surfaces and describe cleavage by number of directions, quality, and angles.

concepts.title: Streak testing and its diagnostic limits
concepts.description: Perform streak tests on unglazed porcelain and interpret color versus hardness limitations for minerals harder than the streak plate.

concepts.title: Specific gravity measurement and heft
concepts.description: Estimate or calculate specific gravity by density relative to water and use heft to distinguish similar-looking minerals.

concepts.title: Mineral color and causes of variability
concepts.description: Distinguish color as a diagnostic property from color variations caused by impurities, structural defects, and trace elements.

concepts.title: Tenacity behaviors and mechanical response
concepts.description: Classify mineral tenacity as brittle, malleable, ductile, sectile, elastic, or flexible and predict response to stress.

concepts.title: Crystal habit and aggregate form terminology
concepts.description: Recognize common crystal habits and aggregate forms including prismatic, acicular, botryoidal, massive, bladed, and granular.

concepts.title: Acid reaction with dilute hydrochloric acid
concepts.description: Test carbonates by observing effervescence with dilute HCl and distinguish calcite, dolomite, and other carbonate minerals.

concepts.title: Magnetism as a diagnostic property
concepts.description: Test minerals for magnetic attraction using a hand magnet and identify magnetite, pyrrhotite, and ilmenite by magnetic response.

concepts.title: Fluorescence and phosphorescence under UV light
concepts.description: Observe mineral luminescence under short-wave and long-wave ultraviolet light and distinguish fluorescence from phosphorescence.

concepts.title: Mineral identification workflow using multiple properties
concepts.description: Apply a systematic sequence of luster, hardness, cleavage, streak, specific gravity, and special properties to identify unknown minerals.

topics.title: Mineral chemistry, classification, and crystal systems

concepts.title: Mineral chemical formulas and stoichiometry
concepts.description: Interpret mineral formulas, calculate oxide/element weight percent, and relate formula units to mineral identity.

concepts.title: Solid solution series and end members
concepts.description: Describe continuous compositional variation between end members using olivine and plagioclase series and predict mineral names from composition.

concepts.title: Polymorphism and polymorph stability
concepts.description: Distinguish minerals with identical composition but different crystal structures and identify stability fields of polymorphs such as graphite/diamond and calcite/aragonite.

concepts.title: Isomorphism and ionic substitution
concepts.description: Predict ionic substitution in mineral lattices based on ionic radius and charge similarity.

concepts.title: Mineral classes by anionic group
concepts.description: Classify minerals into native elements, sulfides, oxides, halides, carbonates, sulfates, phosphates, and silicates based on dominant anion or chemistry.

concepts.title: Silica tetrahedron and silicate polymerization
concepts.description: Describe the SiO4 tetrahedron and how corner-sharing oxygen atoms polymerize tetrahedra into chains, sheets, and frameworks.

concepts.title: Nesosilicate (isolated tetrahedra) structure
concepts.description: Recognize olivine and garnet as silicates with independent SiO4 tetrahedra and explain high density and equant habit.

concepts.title: Single-chain and double-chain silicate structures
concepts.description: Distinguish pyroxene (single chain) from amphibole (double chain) silicate structures and relate cleavage angles to chain geometry.

concepts.title: Sheet silicate structure and basal cleavage
concepts.description: Explain the structure of micas and clays as sheets of linked tetrahedra and predict perfect basal cleavage.

concepts.title: Framework silicate structure in quartz and feldspar
concepts.description: Describe three-dimensional tetrahedral frameworks in quartz and feldspar and relate hardness and lack of cleavage to framework bonding.

concepts.title: Seven crystal systems and unit cell parameters
concepts.description: Classify crystals into cubic, tetragonal, orthorhombic, hexagonal, trigonal, monoclinic, and triclinic systems using axial lengths and angles.

concepts.title: Binary phase diagrams and solid solution behavior
concepts.description: Interpret binary phase diagrams showing solid solution and melting intervals for plagioclase or olivine and predict liquid vs solid compositions during cooling.

topics.title: Mineral formation environments and rock-forming associations

concepts.title: Bowen's reaction series
concepts.description: Apply Bowen's Reaction Series to predict the crystallization order of minerals from cooling magma and explain continuous and discontinuous branches.

concepts.title: Fractional crystallization and magma evolution
concepts.description: Explain how removal of early-formed crystals changes residual magma composition and produces differentiated rock suites.

concepts.title: Pegmatite formation environments
concepts.description: Identify pegmatite bodies as late-stage, water-rich magmatic environments and associate them with large crystals and rare minerals.

concepts.title: Hydrothermal veins and mineral precipitation
concepts.description: Explain how hot aqueous fluids deposit quartz, sulfides, and native metals in fractures and faults.

concepts.title: Metamorphic mineral growth and recrystallization
concepts.description: Explain how pressure, temperature, and fluids cause new minerals to grow in solid state during metamorphism.

concepts.title: Sedimentary mineral formation and evaporite precipitation
concepts.description: Explain how halite, gypsum, calcite, and dolomite precipitate from evaporating water or form by chemical/biochemical deposition.

concepts.title: Weathering and clay mineral formation
concepts.description: Describe how feldspars and ferromagnesian minerals weather to form clays, oxides, and dissolved ions in surface environments.

concepts.title: Common rock-forming minerals in igneous rocks
concepts.description: Identify quartz, feldspar, mica, amphibole, pyroxene, and olivine as primary igneous rock-forming minerals and associate them with felsic or mafic compositions.

concepts.title: Common minerals in sedimentary rocks
concepts.description: Identify quartz, calcite, dolomite, clays, halite, and gypsum as typical sedimentary minerals and link them to clastic or chemical origins.

concepts.title: Common metamorphic rock-forming minerals
concepts.description: Recognize garnet, staurolite, kyanite, sillimanite, andalusite, talc, and chlorite as metamorphic minerals and relate them to protolith composition.

concepts.title: Mineral associations as geologic indicators
concepts.description: Use coexisting mineral assemblages to infer formation environment, protolith, or ore deposit type.

concepts.title: Definition of a rock
concepts.description: Distinguish rocks from minerals and identify rocks as naturally occurring aggregates or masses of minerals, mineraloids, or organic material.

concepts.title: Three genetic rock families
concepts.description: Classify unknown rocks as igneous, sedimentary, or metamorphic based on texture, composition, and observed structures.

concepts.title: Igneous hand-sample identification by grain size and color
concepts.description: Identify common igneous rocks (granite, diorite, gabbro, rhyolite, andesite, basalt, pumice, obsidian, peridotite) using crystal size and color index.

concepts.title: Sedimentary hand-sample identification by grain size and composition
concepts.description: Identify common sedimentary rocks (conglomerate, breccia, sandstone, siltstone, shale, limestone, dolostone, chert, coal) using clast texture and composition.

concepts.title: Metamorphic hand-sample identification by foliation and mineralogy
concepts.description: Identify common metamorphic rocks (slate, phyllite, schist, gneiss, marble, quartzite, hornfels) using foliation type and mineral assemblage.

concepts.title: Polarizing microscope setup and use
concepts.description: Operate a petrographic microscope with plane-polarized and crossed-polarized light and explain how polarizers interact with crystals.

concepts.title: Optical properties in thin section
concepts.description: Recognize relief, birefringence, extinction, interference colors, and pleochroism to identify minerals in thin section.

concepts.title: Thin-section identification of igneous rocks
concepts.description: Interpret photomicrographs of igneous rocks by identifying interlocking minerals and textures such as intergranular, ophitic, and porphyritic.

concepts.title: Thin-section identification of sedimentary rocks
concepts.description: Interpret photomicrographs of sedimentary rocks by identifying detrital grains, cement, matrix, and authigenic minerals.

concepts.title: Thin-section identification of metamorphic rocks
concepts.description: Interpret photomicrographs of metamorphic rocks by identifying foliation, porphyroblasts, and metamorphic mineral assemblages.

topics.title: Igneous rock textures, composition, and settings

concepts.title: Intrusive and extrusive igneous settings
concepts.description: Distinguish plutonic from volcanic settings based on depth of crystallization and infer cooling rates from environment.

concepts.title: Phaneritic texture and slow cooling
concepts.description: Recognize coarse-grained phaneritic texture and explain its formation by slow cooling in plutonic environments.

concepts.title: Aphanitic texture and rapid cooling
concepts.description: Recognize fine-grained aphanitic texture and explain its formation by rapid cooling at or near Earth's surface.

concepts.title: Pegmatitic texture and water-rich residual melt
concepts.description: Identify exceptionally coarse pegmatitic texture and explain growth from water-rich, low-viscosity late-stage melt.

concepts.title: Porphyritic texture and two-stage cooling
concepts.description: Interpret phenocrysts set in a finer groundmass as evidence for two-stage cooling in magma chambers and eruption.

concepts.title: Glassy texture and rapid quenching
concepts.description: Recognize obsidian and pumice as glassy igneous rocks formed by quenching without crystal growth.

concepts.title: Vesicular and scoriaceous textures
concepts.description: Explain vesicle formation by gas exsolution during lava eruption and distinguish pumice, scoria, and vesicular basalt by density and color.

concepts.title: Pyroclastic and fragmental textures
concepts.description: Identify tuff, volcanic breccia, and agglomerate as products of explosive eruptions and fragmented material.

concepts.title: Felsic–mafic–ultramafic composition continuum
concepts.description: Classify igneous rocks by silica content and color index along the felsic, intermediate, mafic, and ultramafic spectrum.

concepts.title: Igneous rock classification diagrams
concepts.description: Use QAPF and color index diagrams to name phaneritic and aphanitic igneous rocks from mineral proportions.

concepts.title: Magma evolution by partial melting, assimilation, and magma mixing
concepts.description: Distinguish how partial melting of source rocks, assimilation of country rock, and mixing of magma bodies alter magma composition.

concepts.title: Volcanic settings and eruption styles
concepts.description: Associate lava flows, shield volcanoes, stratovolcanoes, and calderas with magma viscosity, composition, and tectonic setting.

topics.title: Sedimentary rock textures, composition, and depositional environments

concepts.title: Weathering and sediment generation
concepts.description: Distinguish physical and chemical weathering processes that produce detrital and dissolved sediment.

concepts.title: Clastic, chemical, and biochemical sedimentary rocks
concepts.description: Classify sedimentary rocks as clastic, chemical, or biochemical/organic based on sediment origin and composition.

concepts.title: Grain size scale and clast nomenclature
concepts.description: Apply the Wentworth grain-size scale to classify clasts as gravel, sand, silt, or clay and name resulting rocks (conglomerate, sandstone, siltstone, shale).

concepts.title: Sorting and environmental energy interpretation
concepts.description: Interpret sorting of sedimentary grains as an indicator of transport energy and distance from source.

concepts.title: Rounding and sphericity of clasts
concepts.description: Distinguish angular vs rounded grains and relate rounding to transport distance and abrasion history.

concepts.title: Bedding and stratification
concepts.description: Recognize beds, laminations, and graded bedding as primary sedimentary structures recording depositional events.

concepts.title: Cross-bedding and paleocurrent direction
concepts.description: Interpret cross-bedding geometry to determine ancient current direction and depositional environment.

concepts.title: Ripple marks and their origins
concepts.description: Distinguish symmetrical wave-formed ripples from asymmetrical current-formed ripples and infer environment.

concepts.title: Mud cracks and subaerial exposure
concepts.description: Recognize mud cracks as evidence of wetting and drying cycles in subaerial environments.

concepts.title: Depositional environment identification
concepts.description: Use rock texture, structures, and fossils to identify fluvial, deltaic, eolian, shallow marine, deep marine, lacustrine, or evaporite settings.

concepts.title: Carbonate sedimentary rocks and precipitation
concepts.description: Identify limestone and dolostone and explain formation by carbonate precipitation, shell accumulation, or dolomitization.

concepts.title: Evaporite rocks and mineral sequence
concepts.description: Explain precipitation of halite, gypsum, anhydrite, and sylvite from evaporating brines and identify evaporite rocks.

concepts.title: Lithification and diagenesis
concepts.description: Describe compaction, cementation, recrystallization, and diagenetic changes that transform sediment into sedimentary rock.

concepts.title: Fossils as sedimentary environment indicators
concepts.description: Use fossil type, preservation, and abundance to infer depositional environment and stratigraphic context.

topics.title: Metamorphic rock textures, grade, facies, and tectonic settings

concepts.title: Directed pressure and foliation development
concepts.description: Explain how differential stress aligns platy minerals to produce foliation, slaty cleavage, schistosity, and gneissic banding.

concepts.title: Foliated metamorphic rock sequence
concepts.description: Distinguish slate, phyllite, schist, and gneiss by grain size, foliation type, and mineralogy along increasing grade.

concepts.title: Nonfoliated metamorphic rocks
concepts.description: Identify marble, quartzite, hornfels, and serpentinite and explain why they lack foliation due to composition or pressure conditions.

concepts.title: Index minerals and metamorphic grade
concepts.description: Use index minerals (chlorite, biotite, garnet, staurolite, kyanite, sillimanite) to determine metamorphic grade and isograd boundaries.

concepts.title: Protolith identification and metamorphic changes
concepts.description: Infer protolith from metamorphic mineralogy and texture (e.g., shale to schist, sandstone to quartzite, limestone to marble).

concepts.title: Regional metamorphism and mountain building
concepts.description: Explain regional metamorphism associated with continental collision, subduction, and deep burial over large areas.

concepts.title: Contact metamorphism and thermal aureoles
concepts.description: Describe metamorphism adjacent to igneous intrusions and the formation of hornfels in thermal aureoles.

concepts.title: Dynamic metamorphism in fault zones
concepts.description: Explain cataclastic and mylonitic textures formed by mechanical deformation along faults and shear zones.

concepts.title: Hydrothermal metamorphism and metasomatism
concepts.description: Describe chemical alteration by hot fluids and metasomatic changes that form skarns, serpentinite, and ore deposits.

concepts.title: Metamorphic facies concept
concepts.description: Interpret metamorphic facies as assemblages of minerals stable over specific pressure-temperature ranges (e.g., zeolite, greenschist, amphibolite, granulite, eclogite).

concepts.title: Metamorphic facies series and tectonic settings
concepts.description: Correlate Barrovian, Buchan, and high-pressure facies series with convergent margins, magmatic arcs, and subduction zones.

concepts.title: Porphyroblasts and metamorphic textures
concepts.description: Recognize porphyroblasts, poikiloblasts, and inclusion trails as evidence of mineral growth relative to deformation.

concepts.title: Shock metamorphism and impact features
concepts.description: Identify shocked quartz, coesite, and shatter cones as diagnostic of meteorite impacts.

concepts.title: Rock cycle processes and reservoirs
concepts.description: Identify weathering, erosion, deposition, burial, lithification, metamorphism, melting, crystallization, and uplift as processes that cycle rock material among igneous, sedimentary, and metamorphic reservoirs.

concepts.title: Rock cycle diagram interpretation
concepts.description: Interpret rock cycle diagrams to predict possible pathways and products for any starting rock under given geologic conditions.

concepts.title: Economic uses of igneous rocks
concepts.description: Relate granite, basalt, pumice, and obsidian to construction, abrasives, and landscaping uses.

concepts.title: Economic uses of sedimentary rocks
concepts.description: Relate limestone, sandstone, shale, coal, gypsum, and chert to cement, building stone, energy, and industrial materials.

concepts.title: Economic uses of metamorphic rocks
concepts.description: Relate marble, slate, schist, gneiss, and quartzite to building stone, roofing, flooring, and decorative uses.

concepts.title: Mineral resources and ore deposit types
concepts.description: Identify ore minerals for metals and explain concentration processes forming magmatic, hydrothermal, sedimentary, and residual ore deposits.

concepts.title: Gem varieties and gemstone properties
concepts.description: Distinguish gem varieties of common minerals (corundum ruby/sapphire, beryl emerald/aquamarine, quartz amethyst/citrine) by color, hardness, and clarity.

concepts.title: Industrial minerals and nonmetallic resources
concepts.description: Identify nonmetallic mineral commodities such as gypsum, halite, talc, and kaolinite and their uses in manufacturing.

concepts.title: Fossil fuels as sedimentary resources
concepts.description: Explain coal and petroleum as organic-rich sedimentary resources and relate coal rank to burial and thermal maturity.

concepts.title: Environmental impacts of mining and quarrying
concepts.description: Identify environmental consequences of mineral and rock extraction including acid mine drainage, tailings, and habitat disruption.
